newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Guilder rates quoted touch easier in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Guilder rates quoted touch easier in thin trade.

text.p: Dutch call money was quoted fractionally easier on Thursday but was seen climbing again on Friday when a new special advances pact comes into effect.

Dealers said overnight guilders were a touch lower, quoting at around 2.56 percent bid for most of the session. One securities house was bidding as low as 2.50 percent, level-pegging with the current rate on special advances.
"I expect the rate to bump up again on Friday when the new pact kicks in," one dealer said.
The market was confident the Dutch central bank would leave the rate on advances unchanged at 1600 GMT, dealers added.
A move was extremely unlikely in view of the German Bundesbank decision to fix its equivalent rate, the repo, at an unchanged three percent for the next three weeks, they said.
Three-month guilders were quoted at 2.70 percent bid, down two basis points from Wednesday's 2.72 percent. Trades had been done at 2.75 percent, dealers said.
The guilder was quoting at 112.09 guilders per 100 marks, a touch weaker than Wednesday's 112.08 fixing.
